text: Git branching is a core part of modern version control, especially when working on a team. The main branch, often called "main" or "master," holds the stable version of your project. When you want to add a new feature or fix a bug, you create a separate *feature branch*. This allows you to work freely without affecting the main code. Once your work is complete, you open a *pull request*, which is a request for others to review your changes. After the review and discussion, the branch is *merged*, meaning your changes are officially combined into the main codebase. This workflow keeps the project organized and reduces the risk of errors.
